newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile 1996 banking sector profits up 30.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Chile 1996 banking sector profits up 30.6 pct.

text.p: Chile's banking and financial sector reported net earnings of 289 billion pesos for 1996, up 30.6 percent from 1995, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions reported Thursday.
The profits figure was boosted by a sharp increase in Banco de Chile earnings.

Last year Banco de Chile transferred subordinated debt to a new company that will make repayments under a deal with the Central Bank. Before this deal was struck, Banco de Chile made repayments from its own profits.
The Superintendency figures showed the system reported much more modest profit growth -- just 0.8 percent to 311.5 billion pesos -- before subordinated debt repayments are taken into account.
The sector reported net earnings rose 14 percent in 1995.
Loan portfolios swelled 11.7 percent last year, with commercial credits rising 12.8 percent and consumer loans climbing 34.5 percent, the report said.
Although earnings rose, the sector's return on assets fell as a result of higher costs involved in venturing into new areas of business, as well as greater competition in traditional areas, it said.
"But in any case, this indicator is within satisfactory levels and will present a favorable panorama for the stabilization (of returns) in the long term," it said.
